q: The Grover algorithm for unstructured search (finding a marked element in N items) achieves a quadratic speedup with O(√N) queries. The lower bound matching this is:
opts: Ω(√N) queries — no quantum algorithm can do better (Bennett-Bernstein-Brassard-Vazirani)
exp: BBBV lower bound (1997): any quantum algorithm requires Ω(√N) queries to find a marked element in an unstructured database of N items. Grover's algorithm is optimal. The quadratic speedup (√N vs N classically) is the maximum possible for unstructured search.
